customer involvement in the new service development process is a critical determinant of the operational dimensions of new service performance and a positive antecedent for the market dimensions of new service.

customer involvement is not a panacea for all service development problems but a powerful tool for improving new service performance, especially when it is combined with other factors such as customer orientation and service development capabilities.

customer involvement in the development of new service offerings has positive effects on the operational and market dimensions of new service performance, and that these effects are mediated by the quality of the service and innovation speed.
managers should consider customer involvement as a key driver of new service success, and that they should focus their efforts in the early stages of new service development.
